utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'd like to welcome all and everyone. This is case IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Today we are going to be resuming the cross-examination, but before giving the floor to Mr. Karnavas, the Trial Chamber has rendered an oral decision today pursuant to Pusic's request for extension of time to respond to the motion filed by the Prosecutor relating to judicial notice in Martinovic/Tadic case, has granted the request, and the accused Pusic has now until the 6th of July to file his written submission. Mr. Ibrisimovic, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I only wish to clarify some points. Yesterday, we told the legal officer that this would be a joint submission. We had some technical problems when filing it, so I just wanted to say that it is in fact a joint Defence submission in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So there will be a joint submission by the 6th of July. Mr. Karnavas, let's not waste any more time. It's -- you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Before we begin, a congratulations to the French football team for yesterday's win.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We didn't get to watch it, sir, because we're trying to be as efficient as we can. So we have a lot of material to go through. If you could be as direct as possible, we can get you home and never have to come back again on this case. Yesterday we left off discussing the Livno question, if you may recall.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't finish, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I know. That's where we're going to pick up. That's where we left off. Now, I had shown you a document, and I believe it was document 00117. We had it on the screen, we had both -- both questions there, side by side. If we could pull it up on the screen, and if we could -- it would be on the second page. Just -- again just to remind ourselves. And I don't want to belabour the point, but just to recap from yesterday: The one that was being proposed from the Croats in Livno as an alternative had in it some specific language about a joint state of the constitutive and sovereign Croat, Muslim, and Serbian people. Whereas the one that was passed by the Assembly that ultimately the folks voted on, and as you rightly noted, the Croats in a very large majority voted on, only spoke about a state of equal citizens. We can agree on that; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And peoples.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. And peoples. All right. But that's -- we can agree in principle that that's what the two questions were about; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you -- you told us yesterday that you were not a lawyer, so at least on some occasions you were not able to give us a legal opinion on certain matters, or a legal interpretation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give it to you officially, but I can assist you to understand the difference between these two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm sure you can. My question now, sir, is, during that period of time, did you consult with any legal scholars, constitutional experts? You specifically, being the president of the party, did you consult anyone to see what the differences were so at least you could weigh in on this debate and convince your fellow colleagues that perhaps the question that was being posed by the Assembly would not put the Croatian peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina in any dilemma? That calls for a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it -- and who might those be, those experts? If you want to name names.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among others, the judges of the Constitutional Court, the president of the Constitutional Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could just stick with this document, and if we could just go through the -- some of the debates or some of what some of the folks said, all right? And we would have to go to page 4. I'm just going to cover very quickly. And while we're finding our way through this e-court system, let me preface this area of questioning by reminding us what you told us yesterday, and that is that you did not participate in Livno. You did not attend that meeting. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And if I understood you correctly, you also did not receive or obtain or had any desire, in fact, to even look and see what the record of that meeting was.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither did I have any desire nor did I have an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, you could have -- you could have picked up the phone and requested a copy; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could have.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You could have asked them to fax a copy to you, couldn't you?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I could have, but you don't want to understand one thing: This was after the adoption of the question by the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina. So this move --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to cut you here, because you're not answering my question. We agree -- we agree -- we agree that this is after the adoption of the Assembly. What I want to know is did you make any effort to obtain a copy of the record so at least you could satisfy in your own mind what the conflict, what the debate was regarding the two questions? And it's a yes or no: Did you make any efforts?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't make any efforts because it would have been out of place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And let me just finish on that one. No one prevented you from making any efforts. Because you said it was out of place. There weren't any constitutional provisions, state-wise or party-wise, or even as a human being, there was nothing to prevent you from at least entertaining your curiosity of what might have been discussed on that occasion, given that you, the self-proclaimed dissident, the one that was one of the founding fathers of this political party, okay, did you have any curiosity to find out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas. Your rhetoric is wonderful, but the witness has answered exactly this question exactly and clearly, and I do not see why you always complain about lack of time and then ask three times the same question, with due respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There was a little twist in the answer, but, okay, I'll try to overlook that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let's look at the debate. With respect to Miro Lasic -- you do know who he is; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know best.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. In fact, he is the one that replaced you when you became -- on the Presidency; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Illegally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is that an answer? Yes? He replaced --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he came to that position, but illegally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. And as I understand it, under oath in Kordic you said that he got to that position because President Tudjman along with President Izetbegovic came up with this plan to throw you out because Izetbegovic's term, his second term was coming up and constitutionally he couldn't remain in that position, and therefore since you were the next in line, this was an easy way to get you out of the picture, introduce Mr. Lasic, and that way Izetbegovic could have his third term, and so on and so forth. That's what you testified under oath; right? That's what you believe, and you believe that today as you stand here?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Lasic, also, as I understand - and correct me if I'm wrong, and we'll get to the documents - he was also the individual that was placed in charge to lead the negotiations in Lisbon; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The one that you would requested through an intermediary to be put on on that particular group that would go to Lisbon because you had in a hospital, you were recuperating, and you had communicated a message through a friend to Mr. Mesic that you be placed on that -- on that particular -- that you be part of the delegation; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But instead -- but instead you were noted that Mr. Lasic would be not only one of the delegates but also he would lead that particular delegation during those negotiations; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my goal, for Lasic and not Boban to lead the delegation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it was Boban that went along with Lasic?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the third one was Iko Stanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Iko Stanic; right. And just so we have it for the record, the letter from Mr. Mesic -- we can pull it up, but I believe it was already introduced yesterday as P 00124. All right. Now, let's look at what Mr. Lasic said when the question of Livno was being discussed. And this is on page 4. You might be able to track it along. He says: "Minister of BiH government, presented the view that the referendum question is unacceptable in the part where it mentions cantonisation, which means a territorial definition, and in this respect asked if anyone knew how many thousands of Croats would be living in Serbian or Muslim cantons." So, sir, here we have Mr. Lasic, at least, saying, Listen, this word "cantonisation" should be coming out; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then it goes on -- I'm going to skip part of it, but it ends with: "... Mr. Lasic, adding that the referendum was absolutely necessary because the EU would guarantee the borders of BH, prevent a break-up --" I underscore that myself -- "prevent a break-up which is what some wanted." This is what Mr. Lasic said, the very same individual that went to the delegation in Lisbon and also replaced you on the Presidency of BiH; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, but you should know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- why. Please wait.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- we're just going to go --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me. We're just going to go through what the debate were, what everyone debated at Livno regarding the different questions, and the purpose of this exercise is to show that there wasn't one voice, that this was a democratic process, that this was a debate, one that you might have wanted to participate in, and one that you were not even interested in knowing how the debate went. And the whole purpose goes to your credibility, sir. That's why we're doing this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Object. Object. This is a speech, this isn't a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm trying to assure the gentleman that there's a reason for the questioning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if we could go on to what Mr. -- the next individual stated. I believe it's Zvonar, from Tuzla. He sought clarification on some "... points in the referendum question, and pointed out that cantonisation should not be pursued if there is not a sufficient practical foundation for it." That's what it says; correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that it says here simply goes to counter the interest in the Livno question. You see that both Zvonar and Lasic are talking against it, but you insist on the Livno question. The Croatian people at the referendum gave their answer to the Livno question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to get there. We're going to get there step-by-step. We know what your point is, okay? Then we're going to talk about Saric from Prijedor. He "... insisted that the second part be dropped from the question, precisely the part that refers to cantonisation ..." But then it goes on: "... whereas Iko Stanic, president of the HDZ in Bosanska Posavina, stressed that his region was all for that kind of question." Right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm reading it now just as you are. That's probably correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'm just showing you the democratic process that was going on at the time, sir. Then Pero Markovic of Capljina supported the question but stressed that if he had to take a position on it, he would propose a plebiscite to the Croatian people and that the date of the referendum be postponed. Another point of view; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then we have: "Mr. Bender from Neum, confirmed that the question was politically well formulated and grounded, and said: 'If the discussion of this question produced no answers, let us prepare a plebiscite for the Croatian people.'" Yet another point of view; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to skip some because we don't need to go through all of them. We'll have time to read them. But if we go to the next page: "Perica Juric replied: 'It is precisely the referendum that will decide the position of the Croats in the independent state of BH, and is also the most suitable manner of expression.'" Again, here's another point of view, correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't know what referendum. The official one that we held or the one where they were proposing the Livno question?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: My point, sir, is, as we can see from this document, there were a variety of opinions on how to formulate the question if one was an alternative question or whether to go ahead with the question that was -- that had been adopted. So you had members in the party, some that were for the question as it was, some who wanted it modified with the word "cantonisation" in it, some not with it. Some asking for plebiscite, others not. Correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we go to page 6, so we can leave this document, we see that on page 6 the presiding officer put both questions to a vote, and it says here there were 4 votes in favour of the question adopted at the BH Assembly on 25 January, 140 against, and 3 abstentions. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then there were 140 votes in favour of the question, 3 against, and 4 abstentions, and this is the question that was being proposed during this meeting as an alternative; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it's not clear to you that post festum voting in a party body has no influence on the referendum adopted by the Assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, that's not the point of this exercise. I guess the point of the exercise is -- is to show that at this point in time, at least in party politics, you are indifferent. Perhaps because of your wounded ego, which we'll get to, of what happened up in Zagreb when you were personally attacked by your colleagues for your failures, your incompetent positions, your failure to -- to preside over certain meetings or your positions. I'm not saying that they were right, but this is what happened, okay? But at this point in time, you, in a sense, sir, have deactivated yourself from party politics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Karnavas, I really would like to ask you, like my fellow Judge, Judge Trechsel, that when you are using something like where you said just before, and let me quote, "... that perhaps because of your wounded ego ..." I really do not think that expressions like "wounded ego" should be used when a witness is interrogated. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: There's no question. There's no question, sir. There's no question. Now, if we could just go ahead. Now, we agree that the Assembly -- the question that was adopted by the Assembly ultimately was the one that was voted on. We agree on that; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not the one that was suggested by the Assembly. The Assembly officially adopted that question with the participation of the Croatian delegates.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You're right. I stand corrected in my phraseology. Now, on -- on February 27, 1992, and I'm referring to document -- I guess it would be P 09616. If we could look at this a little bit. This is an excerpt from the meetings -- excerpt from the minutes, okay, from the Presidency of the HDZ. Again, you weren't there at the time, correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it -- but at this point in time, just to make sure that we understand each other, you still believed, at least in your mind, that you were the president, although you had tendered your resignation. You were sort of the resigning president; right? That was your understanding.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how it is according to the statute of the HDZ of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm not talking about what the statute says. I'm asking you what was in your mind. In your mind you still believed that you were the resigning president of this particular political party; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the statute of the Croatian Democratic Union, that's what I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so in that sense -- in that sense, getting back to the earlier meeting in Livno and this one over here on the 27th, one would suspect that you at least would have been participating in these particular meetings; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But they didn't invite me. They had excommunicated me so that they could be the leaders.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And incidentally, because on this particular -- if we look at the minutes, we don't have an acting president. You say they didn't invite you. Are you saying that this meeting took place without your knowledge? You didn't know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. At some point you did find out about it, though, did you not?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always find out from the newspapers what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Good. Now, if we can look at the second page, we see here a decision that was taken by the Presidency. I'm going to read it, the relevant part. It's rather short. And then we can discuss it just very, very briefly. It says here: "The assurances of the European Union expressed on previous occasions as well as during yesterday's talks at the conference of the European Union --"

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Excuse me. I haven't text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll wait for the text.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But it would appear you also understand my reading. First page in B/C/S. All right. "The assurances of the European Union expressed on previous occasions as well as during yesterday's talks at the conference of the European Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina indicate that the result of the forthcoming referendum will not prejudice the future constitutional system of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Likewise, fundamental principles ensuring the sovereignty of the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina in their national regions as well as in the whole of Bosnia-Herzegovina contained in the decision of the Central Board of the HDZ BH in Livno are not disputed." Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then it says: "On the basis of the above, we call on the members of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina and all Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina to fulfil their duty and vote in the referendum." Now, if we could just park here a little bit and discuss it. When it says here "during yesterday's talks at the conference," I suspect what they're talking about are the talks in Lisbon, because if we look at the other documents, your letter to Mesic and Mesic's letter to you, it would appear that the Lisbon conference took place right before this -- this particular meeting of the Presidency; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but Mesic never wrote to me. He wrote to the general secretary, Ivan Markesic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And that's 00124, for the record, P 00124. Now -- and that was the very same meeting that Mr. Lasic was the delegation to, right, that we talked about earlier?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So if we could piece it, the Assembly adopts a question. Some Croats within the HDZ leadership feel that the vital national interests of the Croatian people may not necessarily be protected through this particular referendum question, hence they have the Livno meeting; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Then there is a delegation that goes to the European Union which, as we all know, was the one that required this referendum to take place. A delegation goes, led by one of the individuals who were at this meeting, and two other participants. They come back with assurances from the European Union that they have nothing to worry about, that the question as adopted by the Assembly, okay, will not prejudice the constitutional system of Bosnia-Herzegovina and, likewise, it -- it ensures the fundamental principles of the sovereignty of the Croatian people. So they have assurances that they need not worry; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were their convictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But those were the convictions that were -- those were the assurances that they got from the European Union after having this meeting where they had -- they sat around for a day or so, they discussed the issues, they aired out their problems, and they were told by the European Union, don't worry, be happy, go and vote; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, excuse me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Again, this is overly characterised. Apparently all we're talking about is what is reported on the face of Exhibit 9616. Mr. Kljuic has said he has no other independent knowledge of that, so everything else is Mr. Karnavas's characterisation. We don't know exactly what was said. We don't know exactly what the assurances were. I do agree the document says what it says. That's all we know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then after this, after this date, there was the voting; correct? This -- this meeting that took place after the Lisbon conference, that's dated the 27th of February. And if you recall, when was the date on the referendum? Do you recall that? It was a two-day period.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 29th of February and the 1st of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And in fact, we have evidence, do we not, that the Croatian people went out and voted and voted significantly in favour of the referendum; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely correct. But it wasn't the consequence of the message from these people, because they said that they should go to the referendum, they didn't say how people should vote. We said how people should vote.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I mean, it is -- it is somewhat of a democracy, isn't it? They are telling them to go and vote in the referendum, and as you stated and we all know, the Croats under no circumstances wanted to remain in anything that would have anything to do with the former Yugoslavia. You're shaking your head. Is that yes?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it was very important that they be told that it was for the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I just want to show you one more document just to complete this chapter of our cross, and that's 1D 00398. This from a text on the International Conferences of the Former Yugoslavia official papers, and I just want to share with you -- if we could look on page -- it would be numbered page 24, but in the document I think it's the third or fourth -- fourth page. It starts with B, statement of principles. And at the bottom of the page it will be 1D 190034. If we could just look at -- you can look at the editor's notes first. For the record, the entire volume of both -- I believe it's two volumes, that can be found in the library in this building. If we look at the editor's note, it says: "The following Statement of Principles was agreed upon by the leadership of the three sides of the conflict in Bosnia-Herzegovina in March, 1992. However, it was subsequently repudiated by the Bosnian Presidency." If we go and we read just a little bit into it, it says 1 -- this is: "A. Independence. 1. Bosnia and Herzegovina would be a state composed of three constituent units, based on national principles and taking into account economic, geographic and other criteria." "Bosnia and Herzegovina would continue to have its existing borders and neither the government of Bosnia and Herzegovina nor the governments of the constituent units will encourage or support claims of any part of its territory by neighbouring states. "Sovereignty --" Let me read that word again: "Sovereignty resides in the citizens of the Muslim, Serb, and Croat nations and other nations and nationalities, who realise it through their civic participation in the constituent units and the central organs of the Republic." This was 18 March, 1992. Were you aware of this Statement of Principles, sir?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where? Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, I'm asking were you aware? Were you aware of the Statement of Principles of 18 March, 1992, for New Constitutional Arrangements for Bosnia and Herzegovina? This was done under the auspices of the European Union who at the time were trying to broker a peaceful divorce within the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's the Lisbon document, then I was aware of it, but I only have the English text before me now, which I do understand, but I don't know where that agreement was reached and between which parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But nonetheless, if we look at this document, it talks about sovereignty residing in the nation -- in the citizens of the Muslims. It talks about nations; correct? And at least in principle here we have a Statement of Principles that more or less incorporates -- incorporates some of the concepts and ideas that were part of the Livno question, that Livno debate, even though it wasn't specifically incorporated into the referendum question that was adopted by the Assembly and which people voted on, including the Croats, and which the HDZ supported; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to tell you something. Up until now, you're somebody who has paid greatest attention to the Livno issue in history. Nobody ever gave that document as much importance. You are now keeping me here with the English text -- just a moment, please -- with the English text, you're not telling me where the document originated from, who wrote the document and who signed it, and now you want my comments.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Counsel Karnavas. I have a question. This declaration of principles or Statement of Principles of the 18th of March, 1992, for New Constitutional Arrangements for Bosnia and Herzegovina, who made that agreement, where, when?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This was part --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you ask the witness first whether he was aware of this Statement of Principles, because if you're asking him and he's just looking at it for the first time today, that's a different matter. So you must ask him whether he was aware of it, whether he knew about it. If not, we are facing problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Okay. Let me go step-by-step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At this point in time, sir, you were a member of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, number two, this document, although it's in English but I understand that you read English as well as you understand English, had you seen it before? And as I understand it, it was part of the Cutileiro Plan.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not take part in the negotiations with Mr. Cutileiro.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But I understand this document was generated in Sarajevo on 3/18/1992 -- 18th of -- March 18, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the technical booth kindly be asked to adjust the sound in the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, my colleague -- and I want to thank her very, very much, Ms. Alaburic -- has provided me with the B/C/S copy of it. So perhaps I can have the assistance of the usher, and perhaps we can clear up this dilemma and the gentleman won't think that the high-priced lawyer is trying to pull the wool over his eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could look at the book first. And I've been in quite a few libraries and in people's offices, and I've often seen that particular text. Even though I can't read it, I recognise it. Have you seen this book before, or someone -- or a copy of it?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a book by the son of President Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, can you -- can you look at the page that was shown to you. At least would you verify --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And will you verify for the record whether that version -- and we will copy it for the record, Your Honour, at some point -- but would you verify that that is -- what you're looking at is a translated version of what I've shown you, the Statement of Principles of 18th of March, 1992, signed or agreed upon in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it says here that the text was compiled in Brussels. Secondly, this is the topic of -- of discussion between three national delegations, which I did not participate in, and this is a text that was revoked afterwards because the three national delegations did not agree. It was withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So are you saying that -- first of all, let me back up. My question was: Does it purport to be a translated version of what I have shown you? That's a yes or a no. There's no in between on this one.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same text.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That was the same question I asked you about two questions before. Now, having read this question -- having read the document, okay, and what I'm saying to you, sir, is -- I'm just pointing out that it does contain words such as "sovereignty," right? And "nations" in paragraph -- under Independence, point 3? Does it not have those words in there, sir? I'll read it for you: "Sovereignty resides in --"

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you don't have to read it to me. I can read it. That's what it says, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. If you could answer the question. Thank you. Now, now that we agree what it says, are not these concepts the very same concepts that were being debated, that were being debated in Livno? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were mentioned, but they were never adopted, not the Livno ones or the Cutileiro Plan ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that. But they were being discussed. The point that I'm saying, sir, is these -- this is -- these were concepts that were very --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- there were very dear to the Croatian people; correct? The Croat leadership within the HDZ; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And this, sir, follows, does it not, it follows the Lisbon meeting? I mean, if you look at it chronologically. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And as we noted -- as we noted, the minutes of the meeting of the Presidency followed the Lisbon meeting and preceded the referendum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, just for accuracy's sake. The minutes of -- the Statement of Principles that Mr. Karnavas has shown the witness is dated in -- I believe on the 18th of March, 1992, about two and a half weeks after the referendum, not before the referendum. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me -- let me rephrase the question. You have the minutes of the meeting from the Presidency that preceded the referendum. That's when they -- correct? It's not in the book, sir. The minutes of the meeting of the Presidency --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- was before --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And it was after the Lisbon meeting. And it was after the Lisbon meeting.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there are two proposals of the Cutileiro Plan. You have 38 and 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'll move on. I'll move on. Obviously the gentleman does not wish to cooperate. Now, we'll move on to the next topic. Yesterday, you told us about your political platform, and when I say "your political platform," you kept saying that this was something that it was yours, you had drafted it, and it was something that you could take full credit for; correct? That was the impression that you wanted to give us, or was I mistaken?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I compiled a political platform at which I won the elections and the HDZ convention. So that political platform of mine was accepted as an HDZ programme.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, as I understand it, the political platform is adopted by the Main Board of the party; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First the convention.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. First the convention, and -- but who is on the Main Board? Is it a one-person board? Stjepan Kljuic, board of the HDZ, or are there other members since they have to adopt this political platform? And I suspect there is debate, and some add to it, some subtract part of whatever the proposals are, and they come up with a platform that represents the platform of the party. So who is on this Main Board? If you recall. If you don't, I can get the statute. It's under Article 36, and you can look at Article 35 as well of the statute that set up the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, you must know that that body changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking you whether the body changed. I'm asking you who is on the Main Board. I'm asking for names, if you could just tell us. How many people are on the Main Board?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometimes there were nine, at others 16. Take a look at the documents that you showed. Take the 16th of September, for example, and then you'll see how many were in the Executive Board, how many in the Main Board, and that went on until the convention. At the convention a new leadership was elected, and you have a list of all the members of both the Main Board and the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But my point is it's the board and it's not you that adopts the platform. So it's not your platform, it's the board's platform, and the board represents the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, you led us to believe, and I might be wrong, but there were two instances, one on page 38 of the -- your first day's testimony, which I believe would have been on the 26th of June, and yesterday on page 35 to 36 on a question posed by Judge Trechsel. As I understood, your position is that the political platform did not change. That was your understanding, or your belief, I should say. One that you conveyed under oath to us.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The political platform that was adopted at the convention of the 23rd and 24th of March, 1991, could only have been changed at a new convention, which was never held while I was in the HDZ.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, there were attempts made by some people to change policy over the course of time, and ultimately they succeeded in doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. If we could look at document 00047. I don't -- I believe we might have covered it yesterday, or some parts of it. The Prosecutor did, at least. It's the Main Board of BH HDZ 6 August, 1991. You were still the president of the HDZ, were you not, sir?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it you were still active. You hadn't deactivated yourself or you hadn't been deactivated; right? Still engaged?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we look at the very first page, we have all the names of the participants, and you seem to be the very first, followed by Mate Boban, and so on and so forth; correct? Do you see that? On the very first page on the English version --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we could go -- I don't want to go through the entire one, but the second page we have the agenda, and as in any meeting I suspect there's an agenda; right? It's a pretty organised party, has agendas; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could go to the part called -- page 3, under "Resolutions." Under "Resolutions." And I'm going to -- we're going to go through some parts of it. We'll spend some time. It says -- it starts with: "Which represent the platform of the activities of the BH HDZ in the newly arisen situation were drawn after all proposals and discussions." You see that, sir, do you not? It's right after --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see the text either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Perhaps we can assist you with a -- with a --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we need to have a B/C/S copy. Okay. I can provide you a physical copy if that would help you. All right? Any --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fine, I have one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Super, super. All right. So the first part, it says, "which represent --" "Resolutions which represent the platform --" the platform -- "of the activities of BH HDZ in the newly arisen situation were drawn after all the proposals and discussions." You see that, sir, right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And I take it -- let's go to page -- let's go to the next page, and under point 3. For -- the same page for you. Now, before we get to this, perhaps we might want to talk a little bit about the background of what's going on in the field, what's going on in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is 6 August, 1991. At this point in time, sir, would it be fair to say that not just the political landscape but also the social landscape, the safety landscape in Bosnia-Herzegovina has changed. And by that I mean there's war raging on around, there's panic, there's concern, folks are worried about what is going to happen in BiH; correct? It's not midnight yet, but it's getting close to it.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, so let's get to point 3. Point 3 says, and I'm going to go through this, I'm going to read it, I'll read it slowly: "All the current problems in the field, including internal party conflicts, conflicts between members of different parties or nations, mobilisation of reserve forces, exchange of fire, desertion, movements of the so-called JNA, Yugoslav People's Army, pressing charges against 'persons subject to military conscription,' provocation by individuals, et cetera, should be reported by the municipal boards of the BH HDZ to the secretariat of the BH HDZ in order to take certain preventive political measures." So what I was saying earlier about the landscape, how it had been changed, this more or less talks about that. It gives us a clue of what's going on; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go to the next one, number 4, it says: "The Main Board --" "The Main Board of the BH HDZ states the fact that the Croatian people are in a state of war, and that it has its -- and its territories are subject to direct occupation by Serbia, which is helped by a part of the JNA and other paramilitary Chetnik units." That's correct, is it not, that statement?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And when we're talking about the Croatian people, we're talking about the Croatians living in the Republic of Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Also the Croatian people living in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. I thought I was mistaken. All right, now, number 5: "We recommended --" "We recommend to the BH government to take a decisive --" I'm going to read that once more -- "a decisive and unambiguous position regarding sending recruits to the so-called JNA." So here, sir, they're asking the BH government, of which you were a member of at the time, to take a decisive and unambiguous position; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I was a member of the Presidency. That's a different body. It's not the government. The government is an executive body. Yes, well, we did receive recommendations from the HDZ, and of course the Muslim Bosniak members of the government and Croats were against mobilisation, but the Serbs were in favour of mobilisation. But in August, anyway, we stopped people being sent, the citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina not Serbs being sent to the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Because just to make sure, the government, the executive, doesn't sit on top of the Presidency, does it? It's the Presidency that's above; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll go on to the next one. We're still on point 5, I'm going to skip a paragraph. It says: "The government of BH is requested to stop the mobilisation of the reserve forces in BH." Correct? Because up until that point in time --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Then it goes on: "The government of BH is requested to prevent the 14th Corps of the so-called JNA from coming to BH." Rather ambitious proposal, but -- or recommendation, but nonetheless it was being made; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah, because, let's face it, at that point in time it was rather unrealistic for the government or the Presidency to act on this; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We strove for that, but the fact that we didn't have the forces for it, that's another matter. The army was above civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Then -- and incidentally, by that point in time - and we'll get to it in a little bit - but by that point in time the TOs are more or less stripped of their weapons, are they not? The Territorial Defences.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The weapons were seized earlier on. I assume you know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. So by that point in time other than maybe the police, there's not a whole lot that Bosnia-Herzegovina can do to prevent the JNA, who, as I understand, was a rather formidable and well-organised and well-staffed and well-resourced army; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now we'll skip one, and then it says: "The BH government is requested to use legal means at its disposal and deploy the forces of MUP, Ministry of Interior, to retake the occupied TV transmitter on the Kozara Mountain." So here we're talking about using basically the police, because that's what we're talking about, MUP, Ministry of Interior, that's the police force. Special police, maybe, because we know at some point they were armed with some heavier weapons, but that's what's being requested; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here they say -- the next one says: "If the BH government ignores these resolutions, we shall demand that it be called to account, or possibly to resign." Now, I take it by this point in time folks are getting a little fed up in the HDZ party leadership with the inaction or inability or unwillingness of the Bosnian government to provide safety and security to the good folks who are living in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're not telling the truth. The government did everything it could given the elements it had that took care of citizens, but you must know what the civilian authorities could do faced with a military occupation. So it's not true that the government didn't do this. The fact that the government didn't have the strength to solve the problem, that's an objective difficulty, but to say that the government didn't do anything and that it was indifferent or indolent, that wouldn't be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's work with this a little bit. Let's assume the government did all it could do. It was precious little as far as the folks that were out -- outside of Sarajevo. It was precious little for them, at least, because they weren't sufficiently protected, or at least that's how they felt; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All this is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah. Which would mean that at least if you can't count on the government to protect you, you might as well do something to protect yourself. Maybe not that the government doesn't want to do something, but they cannot under the circumstances. Right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. You're right there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And in fact -- and in fact, for those of us who come from different cultures and from different ways of -- you know, where the government is structured a little bit differently, Tito had -- had already solved this into his game plan, and that's why he had provided not just for the JNA but he had also provided at the very local level, at the municipal level, Territorial Defence systems, so that in the event -- in the eventuality you get cut off from the government, then at the municipality level you would have sufficient arms, and you would have a plan in place so you could self-organise, both politically but also militarily. And that was called the All People's Defence, was it not?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've explained it really well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could go on to the next page, we're going -- I'm going to focus just on point 10. It would be the same page for you. For us it would be -- it's point 10. It says here: "In order to relieve President Stjepan Kljuic from a part of his obligations, the Main Board of BH HDZ authorises the General-Secretary Ivan Markesic, members of the BH HDZ Presidency, vice-presidents of the BH HDZ, and the secretariat of the BH HDZ to act independently in their sphere of work, but with full political and other responsibility." It says that, does it not, sir?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we could park a little bit here, and if we could discuss this just a bit. By this point in time, you as a member of the Presidency are preoccupied with a great deal -- with many affairs, state affairs; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm saying it.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, being part of the Presidency and also being president of a party in this very turbulent time meant that you -- you were stretched in many different directions. Stretched for time, stretched for your ability to focus on issues; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could put it that way, but I am a very calm man.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well -- all right. Now, aside from being calm, it would appear that at least on point 10 what -- a decision is being made that they want to free you up of some of the day-to-day activities, of some of your obligations, and in your stead you have these other members who will act independently in their sphere of work but with full political and other responsibility. So that's a responsibility or -- you're delegating authority at this point in time, or authority is being delegated to these individuals, authority that would normally be under the control of the -- of the president of the party; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I initiated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactamundo. Exactly. That's what I'm saying. In other words, you're telling these folks act independently in your sphere of work and you will have full political responsibility. And I take it some of them did exactly that, that exactly which you asked them to do.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we go on to 14 real quickly - page 5 for you - on 14 it says here that -- there are several appointments of councils, and you're put on the Security Council; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. And then we're going to talk about that in a second, but then on the same point, it says: "The persons in charge must immediately --" underscore immediately -- "submit the list of persons whom they propose for council members at the -- to the secretariat of the -- of the BH HDZ." So you're asked to go ahead and staff immediately and carry on, correct, in your particular councils?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, the security council, if you could tell us, what is that exactly? What did that exactly entail? I think I maybe have a notion of it, but maybe you could help us out here.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the situation, the security council was the most important one. You've seen there were others; legal, health, culture, and others, but this was in view of the situation prevailing in Yugoslavia, especially in Bosnia-Herzegovina, a council that was supposed to take care of the security of the Croatian people, police and military activities, reservists, JNA, and so on, and coordinate all this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, if we go to 16, point 16, it says: "It is considered that the war is gradually being transferred to Bosnia-Herzegovina, so that the HDZ leadership must be constantly alert." And then at the end it talks about introducing a state of emergency, you know. It talks in -- "In order to try to normalise the situation and avoid causing panic in the field, it is considered that there is still no need for BH HDZ to introduce state of emergency in the party," but nonetheless it sounds like this is a clarion call, that the war is coming our way. The winds are blowing southerly, right? And northerly, and westerly; right? You agree with me?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then it goes on: "If there is a direct danger of war in the area, Municipal Board, after consultation with the leadership, will introduce a state of emergency in the Municipal Board of the HDZ." So in other words, HDZ is already putting in the measures in the eventuality so that a state of emergency can be declared; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, if we can just skip to 19. Page 6 for you. 19. We're almost there. It says here: "The Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia-Herzegovina confirms its known position that Bosnia-Herzegovina is a sovereign and indivisible state and its proclaimed principle that BiH -- the BH is a state of Croatian people, together with other peoples, but it will never allow the Croatian people to be treated as a national minority, nor would it allow other peoples to determine the destiny of BH without the influence of the Croats." All right? It says that, does it not?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are very significant theses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Absolutely, because this goes -- this goes to the heart, the core of -- of the Croatian issue prior -- prior to the elections, prior to the break-up of Yugoslavia, because is it not a fact, sir - and I think you as a dissident would agree with me - that there were many Croats that did not wish to be in the former Yugoslavia, and they wanted their own Croatian nation. I'm told that the translation is somewhat --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you understood my English.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood you very well, but you mentioned elections. There were no elections taking place at the time, and that the Croatian people wanted to live in a state and that they wanted their own independent state, well, that -- that was something they had hoped for for eight centuries.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And this was their moment in history.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you must know that many wishes never come true in generations and generations. But we Croats have had the fortune of having two independent states; both Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And within Bosnia-Herzegovina that's where the Croatian nation was one of the constituent nations, correct? Within that geographical space.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All over the territory of the state we were a constituent people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I stand corrected just for -- to make sure the record is clear: When I spoke earlier of a Croatian nation, it's my habit because in America we refer to that as a state, where here, given the context in this particular region, when we're speaking about a nation we're speaking about something different than a state. You would agree with me on that?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And the -- at least the Croatian people as a nation -- as a nation within Bosnia-Herzegovina had been guaranteed by the constitution. You know, it was in the constitution, was it not?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it would appear, sir -- it would appear, sir, and maybe I'm just a little bit off, but it would appear that perhaps if you look at the date, this is 6 August, 1991, and then we look at the date of the referendum, perhaps some folks within the party, within the HDZ leadership thought that the question on the referendum may in part be in contradiction or in collision with paragraph number 19 of this platform resolution, hence why the whole debate.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. By your leave, I'll assist you to understand the situation. The referendum question was about the independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It did not pre-judge the internal organisation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. According to the constitution of 1974, Bosnia and Herzegovina consisted of three constituent peoples; the Croats, the Muslims, and the Serbs, as well as all other citizens. This remained after the referendum. It remained so. This entire process, the Cutileiro Plan, further discussions on cantonisation, all these were simply discussions in which a consensus was sought about the internal ordering of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I think we agree on this. As you well know being in politics --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] Finally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We'll get there. Slowly, slowly. But you would agree with me that reasonable people can often, you know, disagree, and is it not -- would it not be fair to say that at least some of your colleagues, at least because they didn't see the word "sovereignty" or "sovereign nation" in that particular question when in fact it had been part of the party platform, as is stated here on paragraph 19, that might have been a cause of their concern, hence why they at least needed to get that second opinion at Lisbon, and once they were assured, they went ahead. So that's all I'm merely pointing out, is that some of your colleagues may have seen some things a little bit differently than you and could have looked at this paragraph and said, Why aren't those words, "sovereignty," "nation," why aren't they in the resolution? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, these colleagues --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Just answer --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I know you didn't like some of your colleagues, but that's okay.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. On the contrary. They didn't like me. I liked them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Okay. If we get to 22 -- I think we can skip 21, even though it's significant, but we can deal with it later. 22: "We remain behind the policy of independence and indivisibility in BH but should the war start in BH by an attack by Greater Serbia or any other aggressor on the Croatian people in BH, a special plan will be applied." My question, sir, is, when you say "special plan," when the folks that were drafting this resolution of which, as I understand, you signed as president, what did you have in mind when you said "special plan would be applied"?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several variants. We spoke about this at length when discussing the document of the 13th of June in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And that was the plan that you spoke to us yesterday about?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And so there were different options on the table.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depended on how the situation developed on the ground. If you lost the war, you didn't have a chance. If you won a bit, then you did have a chance. Our aim was to preserve Bosnia and Herzegovina. If we could do that, we would have the greatest chance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And if you could not preserve Bosnia-Herzegovina, what was the plan for? What did the plan call for?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that case, we would see what we could do. There was talk about Croats and Bosniak Muslims linking up with the Republic of Croatia together. There was a discussion of the Croats taking the area where they lived as their own community. All these were hypotheses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And so when folks were sitting around talking, as they did, you know, on that particular occasion, I think -- what was it, July 13th was that? And then later on say --

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 13th of June in Zagreb. And this is already the 6th of August --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in Rama.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And these discussions, I take it, went on for some time, because as the war progressed, as the situation changed on the ground, people met, had discussions; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: People were constantly discussing. Nobody slept at all. We were all tense. You're coming from a stable environment, so you are unable to understand the situation psychologically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would -- I would totally agree with you on that one. And I take it such discussions were held -- one example of such discussions, for instance, would be on the 27th of December, 1991, in Zagreb, which you attended. That was one of those sort of discussions where folks talked about the various options; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But it's one thing when somebody discusses options and another thing when somebody assigns only one option.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that. And I don't want to get ahead of myself, but on that particular occasion, on the 27th of December, after speaking of -- after talking about the various options, discussing them, and as I understand it, it was a rather heated -- a rather heated environment where you felt personally attacked, and you voiced it, we can see it in the transcript, the meeting concluded with some sort of a commission being put together, you being part of that commission, the whole purpose of it to begin and -- or actually to continue the discussions along with your counterparts in BiH, in specific the Muslims and Izetbegovic, to see how the situation could resolve in BiH?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Tudjman had, even before this, asked that we negotiate with the Serbs, and we did, but you have to know what the standpoints of our partners were. The Serbs were exclusively in favour of remaining in Yugoslavia at any cost. We were not. The Muslims, or the Bosniaks, were not either. So the problem was how to proceed. That's why there would be a referendum and things would take the course they did. As for us within the HDZ, those people who were personally opposed to me favoured a thesis which later proved to be self-defeating. I'm referring to Kostroman, Kordic, Boban, and so on. On the other hand, as a disciplined man, I asked that a convention be called, and after all this struggle, for you to understand my position, you should know that when I became the president of the HDZ in the former Yugoslavia, it was seen as an Ustasha movement, and only because of my civic image was I able to civilise this movement, which was a wonderful movement, but some Croat officials from the last Communist government did not want to join us. I wanted a convention to be held so I could hand over the party to them and they could continue on their way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. But let me just conclude here because we're about to have a break now. I can finish with this document. If we skip to number 24, it says here: "In order to educate the population for a successful system of defence and self-protection, the secretariat is assigned the task of organising seminars in the field of defence, communications, civil protection." Again, we see, I believe, the HDZ wanting to take actions because they understand that their safety is at risk; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's how I understand it. I read Churchill's memoirs to them about civilian protection or civil defence, for them to prepare it because it was necessary for survival.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And then on 27 you state -- it's stated: "We must be fair and show goodwill in our relations with other people -- with other parties, in order to -- in order not to provoke disorder and incidents." Right? That was part of the party platform.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to recognise the European approach.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And this was the platform as of -- of -- of 6 August, 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the prevailing conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In the prevailing conditions. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I know we're three minutes early, but this concludes this chapter, and we're moving quite slowly but we're getting there. I'll try to pick it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just before we take a break, I have listened to you during this cross-examination, and for over 20 minutes you have put questions to the witness on document 47. As you know, under Rule 90(F) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, the Trial Chamber must monitor the cross-examination of witnesses so that the cross-examination satisfies the Chamber and can unravel the truth and so that we don't waste too much time. I must say I had difficulty in understanding some of the questions that were put to the witness sometimes, and that related to this document. I don't know exactly what you want us to understand in light of these general questions you have put to the witness. If you spend 20 minutes on a document, you are wishing to convey a message to the Bench. As a general rule, one finishes off with a question which wraps up all the other questions that have been put prior to that so that the witness -- so that one understands whether the witness agrees or not. In the questions that were put today, I broke it down into four areas: You addressed the issue of the referendum in paragraph 19 of this document, the attacks launched by the Serbs, and therefore it was important to set up a special plan. This was in paragraph 22. Then the role played by the Croats, the role of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Croats inside Bosnia-Herzegovina, and a number of issues relating to Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia. So there are a number of important issues that are raised, and -- and that you have discussed. I must say I'm a little bit perplexed. After 20 minutes, I'm not quite sure what you were getting at. So that we don't lose any time, what you do, generally speaking, after you've put your question, you sum up with one question which is a way of wrapping it up. As I have said, you've addressed at least four issues, and I find it difficult to find my way around in all of this. Maybe the questions you will ask afterwards will make things clearer, but I just wanted to make sure that I mentioned this to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, Mr. President, there's always room for improvement, first and foremost, and I will be the first one to admit that we strive over here for improvement. Secondly, I have an outline. I usually go from the general to the specific. I will be filling in. Hopefully at the end of the day it will all make sense. Maybe not with this witness but at some other point. It's a step-by-step process. I understand the frustration that perhaps I'm not being as clear as I could be. I will regroup, rethink, I will take your remarks on board, but rest assured, Mr. President, I did not get to watch that very good game yesterday where France was able to win and move forward on the World Cup because I was diligently preparing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. So it is now 10.30. We shall have a 20-minute break and resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have an hour and a half until 12.30. Counsel Karnavas, I give you the floor again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mr. Kljuic, we're going to go on to the next -- the next topic. And just so there's no dilemma about what it's about, it's about the prediction of the conflict in BiH. So we're going to go through a series of documents, and I'm going to step back on date. The last document we dealt with was, I believe, was on August 6th, but I'm going to start with a series of documents. But first, I want to see whether we can agree. As early as April, 1991, and onwards, and it was becoming much -- it was becoming clearer and clearer every day that -- that BH, BiH, Bosnia-Herzegovina, was facing -- was going to face ultimately the JNA and the Serbian aggression, if you want to call it that. Some call it the Chetnik. I prefer not to use that because I think it's a pejorative term, but in any event, as early as April, 1991, it became clear that something was about to happen; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, and just to make -- and this was a discussion, by the way, that was going on within the party, within HDZ.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I don't want to get ahead of myself into the other chapters, but it's fair to say that with this new democratic process in place where you have multi -- a multi-party system, it's one thing to say, okay, let's have a new party. It's another thing to organise it, to staff it, and the day-to-day operation. This was something of a new experience for many of the folks that were engaged in politics at that period of time.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And we're going to talk about some of the challenges that you faced, but suffice it to say there were many challenges, especially you being at the top and, as I understand it, it's rather windy up there, and sometimes the impossible is asked of you. Sometimes folks elsewhere, especially out in the field, don't understand the challenges, don't appreciate the hard work, don't realise how difficult it can be, that it's simply not ordered and done.

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And it would be fair to say that -- and again we'll talk about this a little bit later, but it would be fair to say that at times you were misunderstood by your colleagues, because where they saw no particular result, they may have interpreted as inaction on your part when in fact maybe you were incapable of motivating people or getting things done, not for lack of trying but because of the circumstances; correct?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time there wasn't any of that yet. It's my triumph in Mostar seven days before April. I won at the convention. You heard the results when they were presented by Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. But there's a saying in America that one day in politics you are the toast of the town - people are toasting you - and then the very next day perhaps you may be toast, because politics can be a sort of rough game, especially when people are getting to learn how to -- how to exercise or how to play within the new rules of the game; right?

utterances.speaker: STJEPAN KLJUIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And it's very important how many times you rebound, get back up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I agree. Now, getting back to the topic that we're going to talk -- that we will be discussing, which is predicting the conflict, I'm going to go through a series of documents just very quickly. The first one is dated 4 April, 1991, 00032, I believe. P 00032. Extract of minutes. And while this is being placed on the monitor, I'll begin. Here you are present along with others.
